newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles down despite higher cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles down despite higher cash.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished lower Friday despite higher spot cash market prices in the western U.S. triggered by forecast of below-normal temperatures in the region next week.
There was little news in today's market to buck current bearish sentiments prompted by concerns over abundant resources for hydroelectric production well into the spring.
The electricity complex struggled toward higher levels in afternoon trading, but ultimately failed.
February California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled down 33 cents at $13.70 a megawatt hour (MWh) after bouncing in a 50 cent range.
March COB finished down 65 cents at $12.20 after setting a new life-of-contract low at $12.10.
February Palo Verde (PV) futures settled down 10 cents at $16.45 after traded between $16.35 and $16.65. March PV finished down 45 cents at $14.40.
"There's more pressure on March than February because of stronger prescheduled prices," a Houston futures trader said.
Peak, firm electricity for Monday delivery at COB rose three dollars from Thursday's levels to $16.50-$17.50 and at PV climbed two dollars to a $19.00-$20.00 range Thursday.
Temperatures in the Northwest were expected to average 3-10 degrees Fahrenheit below normal into early next week, while those in the Southwest were predicted to to average 4-8 degrees below normal.
The latest weather outlook showed a mild weather system would arrive into the West by the end of next week.
Most brokers and traders expect the complex to continue testing lower levels Monday.
"Depending on when the hydro hits...they're fairly valued at current levels," said a western futures trader.
